instruction: Replace all "students" with "learners" and all "educators" with "teachers" in this document.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully used VS Code Find & Replace (Ctrl+H) to replace all 'text' with 'test' in the document and saved the file. Completed in 9 turns.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can open VS Code Find & Replace dialog, type search/replace terms, execute Replace All, and save the file.
metadata.task_rationale: Harder variation requiring two separate find-and-replace operations. Tests whether model can perform multiple sequential replacements using the same Find & Replace dialog.
metadata.explanation: Task requires two replacements: 'students'→'learners' (2 occurrences) and 'educators'→'teachers' (1 occurrence). Partial credit: 0.5 for each replacement pair completed correctly.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads file content from the target path after postconfig saves the file with Ctrl+S
Metric correctly handles expected parameter - directly accesses 'replacements' from the rules dict without the common 'expected.get("rules")' anti-pattern
Both replacement pairs (students→learners, educators→teachers) are verified, providing complete coverage of the instruction
Partial credit logic (0.5 per replacement pair) is well-designed and matches the scoring breakdown
Each replacement is verified with dual check: old word absent AND new word present at least expected_count times
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: case-sensitive matching could miss capitalized variants (e.g., 'Students') if they exist in the document, but this matches the instruction's exact wording so is acceptable
Minor: if 'teachers' or 'learners' pre-exist in the document, the count check could produce false positives, though the combined old_gone AND new_present check mitigates this well
